name: Question 10
worked_solution:
First, notice that

$$
{[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2} & -\frac{1}{2} \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

So, we have been given the following diagonalization of $A:$

$$
A={{[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{P}{{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{D}{{{[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}}_{⏟}}_{{P}^{-1}}
$$

Since $A=PD{P}^{-1}$, we can compute ${A}^{k}$ by using the formula 

$$
{A}^{k}=P{D}^{k}{P}^{-1}.
$$

Carrying out the necessary multiplication, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{101} & =P{D}^{101}{P}^{-1} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}]}^{101}(\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}]) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{1}^{101} & 0 \\ 0 & (-1)^{101}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

First, notice that

[2101]−1=[12−1201]=12[1−102].

So, we have been given the following diagonalization of A:

A=[2101]⏟P[100−1]⏟D[2101]−1⏟P−1

Since A=PDP−1, we can compute Ak by using the formula Ak=PDkP−1.

Carrying out the necessary multiplication, we obtain the following:

A101=PD101P−1=[2101][100−1]101(12[1−102])=12[2101][110100(−1)101][1−102]=12[2101][100−1][1−102]=12[2−10−1][1−102]=[1−20−1]
